  "summary": "This archival unit contains J. B. Kripalani’s typed letter of 3 June 1963 to Minoo Masani, written from Lucknow, together with an enclosed typescript of Kripalani’s inaugural address at the PSP–SP Unity Conference in Lucknow on 1 June. In the letter, Kripalani congratulates Masani on the success of “Shakuntala” in Bombay, reports recent discussions with Dr. Rammanohar Lohia, and asks Masani to help determine the next steps toward a public discussion and meeting of democratic opposition leaders, including C. Rajagopalachari and Jayaprakash Narayan.\n\nThe enclosed address presents a broad critique of India’s condition in 1963. Kripalani argues that Five-Year Plans have not improved mass living standards, while agriculture has stagnated, food imports and prices have risen, taxes have increased, and public administration has deteriorated. He links these failures to the Congress’s prolonged dominance, the weakening of democratic checks, and the difficulty of building an effective opposition. His proposed remedy is unity among democratic opposition parties around a minimum common programme: efficient administration, resistance to Chinese aggression, improved India–Pakistan understanding, social justice, restraint on further nationalisation until the public sector is efficient, and effective control of private enterprise.",
